title: SRH teammate says Cummins will turn up for IPL
excerpt: Additionally, Josh Hazlewood and Cameron Green are expected to be available for their respective franchises
author: Vijay Tagore
body: Pat Cummins, at the centre of the resurfaced Sandpapergate controversy, is expected to feature in IPL 2027. The Australia captain, who received a vote of confidence from Cricket Australia (CA) on Saturday, is believed to have confirmed his availability for the season, even as a couple of key Australian players have opted out, citing workload concerns. Josh Hazlewood, however, will turn up for Royal Challengers Bengaluru.

Cummins is the captain of Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH), and the fact that the franchise has not released him is an indication of his availability. Now, a senior member of the side has also confirmed that he is expected to turn up. “I have spoken to Pat and he has said he will come for sure, if not for the whole season, at least for a part of it,” the member, who is currently part of the ILT20 in the UAE, told Cricbuzz.

It has also been the franchise's consistent position that the skipper would be available for the season, which was why he was not released. Cummins featured in only part of last season, joining the team in the second half after receiving a late go-ahead from CA. He played eight games, with Ishan Kishan leading the side in his absence.

Cummins' availability was in doubt because of Australia's packed international schedule on either side of the IPL. Australia are scheduled to play nine Tests before the IPL, including five against India between January and March, followed by a five-Test Ashes series against England immediately after the league, from June to August. However, those doubts over his participation have now been put to rest.

SRH, however, have had to release Head after the opener decided to focus on family and international commitments. Delhi Capitals are in a similar situation, having had to release Mitchell Starc after the pacer expressed his inability to take part in the season. The veteran quick wants to manage his workload.

However, Hazlewood is believed to have conveyed his availability to Royal Challengers Bengaluru, the two-time defending champions. Cameron Green, too, is expected to be available for the season, according to Kolkata Knight Riders, who retained him. “We have been told that he will come for the season,” a KKR official said, explaining the decision not to release the all-rounder, who was bought by the franchise for a whopping Rs 25.20 crore at the last auction.
